# Walmart.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/walmart-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/walmart-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product listing data from Walmart.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Walmart.com Product Data (2025 Update)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-walmartcom)
- **Code:** [`walmart.py`](walmart.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Product pages](results/products.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Walmart Product pages
- Walmart search pages

## Functions

- `scrape_products(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: Scrape product data from product pages with a JS rendering fallback.
- `scrape_search(query='', sort='best_match', max_pages=None)`: scrape single walmart search page

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import walmart


async def main():
    products = await walmart.scrape_products(
        urls=[
            "https://www.walmart.com/ip/1736740710",
            "https://www.walmart.com/ip/715596133",
        ],
    )
    search = await walmart.scrape_search(query="laptop", sort="best_seller", max_pages=3)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/products.json`](results/products.json): `product`, `reviews`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `__typename`, `buyBoxSuppression`, `similarItems`, `id`, `usItemId`, `isBadSplit`, `fitmentLabel`, `name`, `checkStoreAvailabilityATC`, `seeShippingEligibility`, `brand`, `type`, `shortDescription`, `weightIncrement`, `topResult`, `additionalOfferCount`, `availabilityInNearbyStore`, `itemBeacon`, `catalogProductType`, `conditionPriceRange`, `imageInfo`, `aspectInfo`, `plItem`, `canonicalUrl`, `conditionV2`, `externalInfo`, `itemType`, `category`, `returnPolicy`, `badges`, `buyNowEligible`, `classType`, `averageRating`, `numberOfReviews`, `esrb`, `mediaRating`, `salesUnitType`, `sellerId`, `sellerName`, `sellerType`, … (80 more)

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`walmart.py`](walmart.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/walmart-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
